monitor.horizonStripTitle: How to read CSI 300 (long only — you cannot short)
monitor.horizonMeaningShortBull: Recent days are firm; they do not size the book
monitor.horizonMeaningShortChop: The last few days are mixed — not a sizing call
monitor.horizonMeaningShortBear: Recent days are weak; that alone does not flatten
monitor.horizonMeaningMediumBull: Index is up; still do not add this theme
monitor.horizonMeaningMediumChop: Buy dips / sell highs in names
monitor.horizonMeaningMediumBear: Do not buy new names today
monitor.horizonMeaningLongBull: Price is above the year line
monitor.horizonMeaningLongChop: Year line intact — not a bear market
monitor.horizonMeaningLongBear: Below the year line, still not a bear-market verdict
monitor.horizonHeadlineMediumLongBear: Medium is soft-bear, so do not buy new names today. Long soft-bear only means the year line is broken — not that a bear market is confirmed.
monitor.horizonHeadlineMediumBear: Medium is soft-bear: no new buys today. The year line is not broken, so this is not a bear market; keep or trim what you already hold.
monitor.horizonHeadlineMediumBull: The index is in a medium uptrend, but that historically does not lift this theme — still no adds.
monitor.horizonHeadlineShortBearChop: Only the last few days are weak. Sizing follows the middle box, which is still range-bound: buy dips, do not flatten.
monitor.horizonHeadlineChop: Range is the default. Buy dips and sell highs in names. A real soft-bear needs a down-stacked tape and a negative half-year return.
monitor.horizonHowToMediumLongBear: To flip back: a close above the 60-day line ends the medium soft-bear; a close above the year line ends the long one. A classic bear market usually also needs ~20% off the peak.
monitor.horizonHowToMediumBear: A close back above the 60-day line returns medium to range. While the year line holds, 0% means no new buys — not a broker flatten.
monitor.horizonHowToMediumBull: Short-term strength or weakness only explains the last few days; it does not change “do not add this theme.”
monitor.horizonHowToShortBearChop: Short-term flip: close back above the 5-day line. Sizing still follows the middle box.
monitor.horizonHowToChop: A real soft-bear needs the 20/60/120-day averages stacked down, a close under the 60-day line, and a negative half-year return.
monitor.horizonMediumDrives: Sizing follows the middle box. The last few days only explain noise; the right box asks if this is a bear market. Wait / 0% = no new buys today, not a broker flatten.
monitor.hintHorizonShort: 5/10/20-day averages. A two-day drop is short-term weakness. It does not zero the book by itself.
monitor.hintHorizonMedium: Roughly 1–6 months. This is the shared add gate: soft-bear = do not buy new names today.
monitor.hintHorizonLong: Close vs the year line. Breaking it is a caution, not “bear market confirmed.” A classic bear usually also needs ~20% off the peak.
